text.p: Benazir Bhutto said on Tuesday she rejected the outcome of Pakistan's elections, in which her Pakistan People's Party (PPP) suffered a crushing defeat.
"I don't accept the results," she told a news conference, saying Monday's polls had been massively rigged.
Bhutto said PPP leaders would meet in Islamabad on Wednesday to discuss whether successful party candidates should take up their National Assembly (lower house) seats.
"The party will decide whether they will sit in the assembly or not," she said. "There is a lot of anger and protest in the party. The people have been defrauded."
"I don't think I have been defeated. I think I have been cheated," she said. "The people are groaning."
Bhutto accused the Election Commission of giving out inaccurate voter lists, allowing some polling stations to open late and close early, and failing to announce results promptly.
Foreign election observers have acknowledged there were some irregularities in voting procedures, but say they detected nothing that would have changed the outcome.
Bhutto said she derived "quiet satisfaction" from what she called President Farooq Leghari's failure to form his own parliamentary bloc and move Pakistan towards presidential rule.
Leghari has denied harbouring any such ambitions.
Bhutto said she had no plans to launch popular agitation against a Sharif government, saying this was not the moment to force another election on an exhausted nation.
"For better or worse, Sharif and the PML have been given a charge of this country," she said. "They have in effect been given a blank cheque to rewrite the constitution."
She said irrespective of her views concerning the legitimacy of the electoral process, she wished Sharif good luck.
"The country needs political stability, our people need economic relief. The two go hand in hand," she said.
"For the sake of the people of Pakistan, for their economic betterment and for the sake of parliamentary democracy, I hope that we have political stability," she said.
Bhutto denied that corruption had flourished under her government, as alleged by Leghari when he fired her in November.
"I am very proud of my performance. I have been the best prime minister," she declared.
